properties.title: Learning response-aware patient dynamics for respiratory support

properties.name: Response-aware respiratory patient dynamics (arXiv v3)
properties.membership: Core learned action-conditioned physiological world model
properties.architecture: History/static encoders initialize latent state; baseline+gated treatment-associated delta; response encoder and recurrent latent update carry generated physiology six hourly steps. Room-air soft regularizer is an observational reference, not causal identification.

properties.design: Retrospective deidentified adult ICU EHR; internal development/validation, later-period temporal cohort and independent-institution external cohort; six-hour histories forecast six hours under recorded support actions.

assertions.rationale: History and static encoders initialize latent state.
Binary observed/imputed indicators and action availability masks enter model.
Separate TSLM variables provided to initial encoder.
Training-derived preprocessing fixed for validation/external; temporal/independent-cohort boundaries declared. Availability-clock audit remains unreported.
Dynamic history and separately encoded static patient features combine for initial state.
Observed/imputed measurement status and treatment setting availability are explicit inputs; unavailable settings encoded zero plus mask.
Latent state recursively updated using prior state, generated physiology, action and encoded delta.
Six-hour physiological and support history initialize forecast.
History encoder plus recurrent state retain prior history through horizon.
Recorded support modality and settings are supplied separately to each transition.
Therapeutic respiratory support is distinct from measurement features; modalities roomair/O2/HFNC/NIV.
Onehot support/subtype plus FiO2,flow,IPAP,EPAP and setting masks define treatment inputs.
Hourly support sequence conditions a six-hour forecast.
Residual physiology update and recurrent latent update advance hourly state.
Learned encoders, baseline/treatment networks and recurrent update trained with masked multistep MSE.
Generated states carried across all six forecast steps during training.
Residual delta readout maps latent state into next50 physiological values.
Physiology forecast output has explicit hourly variable targets.
Generated physiological states feed subsequent state and delta steps.
Maximum evaluated six hours, hourly predictions.
Recurrent internal state updated each generated physiological step.
Support-conditioned forecasting evaluated across internal/temporal/external cohorts.
One-hour errors reported alongside longer forecast horizons.
Common free-running protocol reports per-hour RMSE1–6.
Hourly successor physiology compared to observed targets. Evaluation is reported; this annotation does not establish a formal categorical acceptance outcome, so no pass/fail result is inferred.
Free-running generated trajectories evaluated across six hours. Evaluation is reported; this annotation does not establish a formal categorical acceptance outcome, so no pass/fail result is inferred.

Later-period, independent-institution and support-stratified tests reported. Evaluation is reported; this annotation does not establish a formal categorical acceptance outcome, so no pass/fail result is inferred.
Evaluated rollout explicitly receives no future physiological measurements/observed responses.
Study explicitly limits itself to observational forecasting; no matched alternative-treatment results.
Treatment recommendation/decision modeling is future work, not an evaluated pathway.
No policy/search optimization reported; future decision modeling explicitly proposed.
Authors explicitly deny causal-effect identification and discuss observed confounding.
Conditional decomposition is explicitly not an identified respiratory treatment effect.
Implementation release is future tense; no present source-repository release identified.
Research-only short-term physiological forecasting, explicitly not autonomous support selection.
IRB approval/consent waiver reported, but named institution/protocol identifier not supplied.
criteria_met: Retrospective approval/waiver claim and data-governance scope

evidence_fragments.content:
We represent the patient using a latent state that is updated over the prediction horizon. The model has four main
components: (1) initialization of the latent patient state from recent history, (2) state-dependent encoding of respiratory
support, (3) decomposition of predicted physiological change into baseline dynamics and respiratory-support-associated
deviations, and (4) response-aware latent-state updating using the predicted physiological change. An overview of the

evidence_fragments.content:
We conducted a retrospective study using de-identified EHR data from adult ICU patients (≥18 years). Data
from January 1, 2016, to December 31, 2023, were divided into a development cohort (Dev) for model training and an
internal validation cohort (Val) for model selection. We additionally evaluated the model on a later-period cohort from
the same institution (Temporal; January 1, 2024–June 30, 2024) and an independent cohort from a separate institution
(External; January 1, 2023–August 31, 2024). All analyses were conducted under institutional review board approval
with waiver of informed consent. Cohort characteristics are summarized in Appendix Table 4, with cohort construction
and preprocessing details provided in Appendix B.

deterioration [Roca et al., 2019]. Performance is evaluated only at observed target measurements.

Continuous respiratory support settings consisted of FiO2, oxygen flow, IPAP, and EPAP. These settings are not
applicable to every respiratory support modality. For example, flow may be available for high-flow oxygen support,
whereas IPAP and EPAP are primarily associated with non-invasive positive-pressure ventilation. We therefore paired
each continuous setting with a binary availability mask. For a treatment setting qt with corresponding mask rt, only
training observations satisfying rt = 1 were used to estimate its normalization statistics. When the setting was available,

value of zero while the availability mask remained zero, which allows the model to distinguish an unavailable treatment
setting from an observed value whose standardized value happens to be close to zero.

evidence_fragments.content:
External cohorts were transformed using exactly the same preprocessing parameters
estimated from the internal training cohort. In particular, missing physiological observations were imputed using the
internal training medians, physiological variables were normalized using the internal training means and standard
deviations after imputation, and respiratory support variables were encoded using the treatment vocabulary and
continuous-setting normalization parameters learned from the internal training cohort. No preprocessing parameters
were re-estimated on external data, which ensured that external evaluation reflected deployment of a fixed model and
fixed preprocessing pipeline to previously unseen patient populations.

capability_assessments.rationale: Implemented persistent latent state, learned temporal transitions and evaluated recorded-action-conditioned six-hour trajectories meet L2. No matched alternative-action experiment establishes L3; no policy optimization establishes L4. Observational conditioning is not treatment-effect identification.

legacy_cells.B: Learning response-aware patient dynamics for respiratory support
legacy_cells.S: Forecast the next six hours of patient physiology given recent physiological history and recorded respiratory-support actions.
legacy_cells.T: Adult ICU patients (≥18 years); retrospective development, temporal, and independent external cohorts.
legacy_cells.AI: Hourly physiological measurements; respiratory-support modality and settings; measurement-availability indicators and time-since-last-measurement; static demographic, clinical, and comorbidity variables
legacy_cells.AN: Median imputation for missing physiological values; retain missingness indicators and time-since-last-measurement features.
legacy_cells.BD: Respiratory-support modality and device subtype; FiO2, oxygen flow, IPAP, and EPAP settings with availability masks.
legacy_cells.BL: Hourly bins; six-hour observed history and six-hour prediction horizon.
legacy_cells.BV: Masked multi-step trajectory-prediction MSE plus λRA-weighted L2 penalty on the respiratory-support-associated deviation during room-air steps; response-guided warm-up during initial training.
legacy_cells.DX: Table 2 reports 1-h RMSE: proposed model 0.361 (validation), 0.389 (temporal), and 0.620 (external); corresponding MedDreamer-WM values 0.344, 0.369, and 0.610.
legacy_cells.DY: Table 2 overall RMSE: proposed model 0.516 (validation), 0.550 (temporal), 0.880 (external); 6-h RMSE 0.619, 0.653, and 1.062, respectively. On meaningful-change targets (Table 3), RMSE was 1.016, 1.105, and 1.771, with reported improvements over persistence of 10.1%, 9.7%, and 4.2%.
legacy_cells.EI: Compared with Persistence and Action-GRU (Table 2). Overall RMSE: proposed model 0.516 vs 0.549 and 0.520 (validation); 0.550 vs 0.587 and 0.552 (temporal); 0.880 vs 0.901 and 0.880 (external).
legacy_cells.EJ: Compared with SepsisAgent-WM and MedDreamer-WM (Table 2). Overall RMSE: proposed model 0.516 vs 0.519 and 0.516 (validation); 0.550 vs 0.552 and 0.550 (temporal); 0.880 vs 0.878 and 0.889 (external).
legacy_cells.EK: Ablated base dynamics, addition of respiratory-support-associated dynamics, and the full model with response-aware state update (Table 1).
legacy_cells.EO: Uses de-identified EHR data; authors state that underlying clinical data cannot be publicly released where institutional policies or data-use agreements restrict release.
legacy_cells.ER: Institutional review board approval; informed consent waived.
legacy_cells.FB: Latent patient state initialized from a six-hour history of 50 hourly physiological variables, respiratory-support history, measurement availability/time-since-last-measurement, and static demographics, clinical variables, and comorbidities; latent dimensionality is not specified in the extracted text.
legacy_cells.FL: Sequence encoder initializes a latent patient state from physiological history, respiratory-support history, measurement timing/availability, and static covariates. A state-dependent support encoder feeds a transition that sums baseline physiological change and gated support-associated deviation; a response encoder processes predicted change, and a state-update module recursively updates the latent state. Outputs are predicted physiological trajectories; no planner is evaluated.
legacy_cells.FM: Introduces response-aware respiratory-support forecasting that decomposes predicted physiological change into state-dependent baseline dynamics and support-associated deviations, then uses the predicted change in latent-state updating; analyzes room air as the reference condition.
legacy_cells.FN: The model had comparable overall trajectory-prediction performance to baselines across validation, temporal, and external cohorts. On meaningful-change targets, its RMSE improvements over persistence were 10.1%, 9.7%, and 4.2%, respectively.
legacy_cells.FO: The study is retrospective and observational, not treatment-effect estimation or treatment recommendation; treatment assignment may depend on measured and unmeasured factors; generalization may be limited by institutional and population differences; prospective validation and failure-mode assessment remain needed.
legacy_cells.FP: Investigate counterfactual trajectory analysis and respiratory-support decision modeling, with explicit treatment of confounding and prospective validation.
legacy_cells.FQ: Existing action-conditioned patient-dynamics models typically combine physiological progression and intervention-associated change in one transition and do not explicitly represent physiological change during state updating.
legacy_cells.FR: Action-conditioned forecasts and the room-air-anchored decomposition do not identify causal treatment effects; no counterfactual comparison of alternative support sequences for the same patient, treatment recommendation, planning result, or prospective clinical benefit is demonstrated.
